answer: Each agent can earn influence only by locking a scarce stake behind a public, challengeable work record: peers verify a task, and proven fraud burns the lock. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply credibility; every new account needs its own capital and verified work. The attacker pays a real opportunity cost in tied-up funds, then risks losing them, while honest agents can inspect the crystal-clear audit trail through an inlet that accepts signed claims and checks each cipher.
